title: An engine that refuses is not an engine that is slow
blurb: Every path that reported a failed search ended with the same sentence — that is usually temporary, try again — which is true of a timeout and false of the most likely first experience of a configured engine: SearXNG answers 403 to every query until an instance opts into JSON, so a first run refuses everything, permanently, and the report recommended waiting. Three faults now, split on whether the engine answered at all, which is HTTP's rule rather than a guess about one provider. A reader is told only whether asking again is worth anything; the variable, the file and the status code go to whoever is holding the terminal. Running it against a refusing server found the surface no test reached: the whole-run refusal, which renders from a kind rather than a sentence.
